extracted.intended_audience: Participating Clubs, Club Affiliates, Team Delegation Members and their contracted third parties for the FIFA Intercontinental Cup 2025
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and standards governing media, marketing, equipment, sponsorship, advertising, wearable tech, training-site and matchday media activities that Participating Clubs and their affiliates must follow during the FIFA Intercontinental Cup 2025.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorisations for use of player information
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Participating Club shall secure any and all necessary authorisations for FIFA to use information about the players of the Participating Clubs (such as players’ statistics – height, weight, age, etc.) as well as details of the Participating Club’s history in connection with its participation and that of its Team Delegation Members in the Competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clubs must obtain the required permissions from players and other data subjects so FIFA may use personal/statistical and historical club information in relation to the Competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ownership of Competition Marks
rubrics_metrics.description: FIFA is and remains the sole owner of all of the Competition Marks, and retains the sole right to develop any marks, logos and symbols for and/or in connection with the Competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participating Clubs must recognise FIFA's exclusive proprietary rights over Competition-related marks and branding.

rubrics_metrics.name: No development of competing marks
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Participating Club must ensure that neither itself, nor any of its Club Affiliates, nor any third party contracted to a Participating Club, develops, uses, registers, adopts or creates any mark, logo or symbol which refers to the Competition, or which is in FIFA’s reasonable opinion confusingly similar to, is a colourable imitation of, a derivation of, or which unfairly competes with any of the Competition Marks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically refrain from names/logos/terms that the public may infer identify FIFA or the Competition (examples listed: 'Intercontinental Cup', 'Copa', 'Cup', 'Coupe', 'Pokal', 'FIFA', 'Copa Intercontinental', 'IP', 'Interkontinental-Pokal' or translations) or from using dates in conjunction with territory/venue names that could identify the Competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: No challenge to Competition Marks
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Participating Club undertakes not to oppose, and to ensure that none of its Club Affiliates or contracted third parties oppose, any of the trademark or copyright applications filed by FIFA, Commercial Partners or other affiliates authorised by FIFA, nominees or licensees in respect of the Competition Marks, or seek to cancel any such registrations held by FIFA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clubs must not apply for copyright/trademark/patent protection or domain names that would adversely affect FIFA’s proprietary interests; if a Club Affiliate or third party opposes FIFA filings the Participating Club must ensure immediate desistance. Exception: pre-existing IP rights registered prior to publication of these regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambush marketing prohibition (anti-infringement undertaking)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Participating Club is required to ensure that its Club Affiliates and further contracted third parties i) do not directly or indirectly become (or seek to become) associated with FIFA, the Competition, or any other competition or event organised by, or under the auspices of, FIFA; ii) do not exploit the goodwill of the Competition, FIFA, or any other competition or event organised by, or under the auspices of, FIFA; and iii) comply with the provisions of these Media and Marketing Regulations regarding the use of the Competition Marks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clubs must prevent, monitor and stop any Ambush Marketing activity by affiliates or contractors that exploits or seeks association with FIFA/Competition goodwill or marks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to Participating Clubs of violations
rubrics_metrics.description: FIFA will notify a Participating Club if any of its Club Affiliates, or any third party contracted to the Participating Club, is conducting any activity which, in FIFA’s reasonable opinion, constitutes a violation of these Media and Marketing Regulations, including but not limited to: (i) an infringement of FIFA’s Intellectual Property Rights; (ii) an unauthorised competition, sweepstake or promotional activity involving Competition tickets or access to Official Training Sites; (iii) an infringement of restrictions on activities of Club Affiliates or contracted third parties as described; or (iv) any other Ambush Marketing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification will identify alleged violations including the four categories above; clubs should expect FIFA to raise such issues and to act accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of ambush marketing provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions prohibiting Ambush Marketing apply even if the infringing activities are not directly connected to the relevant Club Affiliate’s or contracted third party’s association with the Participating Club.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clubs are responsible for affiliate/contractor actions regardless of direct connection to competition participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cessation and undertakings following ambush marketing notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Following written notification by FIFA of any Ambush Marketing or any further violation by any Club Affiliate or any third party contracted to a Participating Club, each Participating Club will ensure, and take all measures required by FIFA to ensure, that the relevant Club Affiliate or contracted third party immediately ceases and desists and provides FIFA with written undertakings to refrain from future occurrences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clubs must secure immediate cessation and written commitments from offending entities; applies to affiliates and their group companies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring and reporting obligation by Participating Clubs
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Participating Club shall use its best efforts to monitor the advertising market in its home country for any Ambush Marketing conducted in that market and shall promptly notify FIFA about any such activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Active market monitoring and prompt reporting to FIFA are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term of the Media and Marketing Regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: These Media and Marketing Regulations take effect from 2 October 2025 and remain in force for the entire Competition Period, including Matchdays and non-Matchdays, and expire on the last day of the Competition Period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All obligations apply throughout the defined effective period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive FIFA rights – Media
rubrics_metrics.description: FIFA has the sole and exclusive right to exploit any and all Media Rights in relation to the Competition. Except where expressly authorised by FIFA, neither the Member Associations, nor the Participating Clubs, nor the Hosts, nor the Confederations, nor any third party may exploit any Media Rights or parts thereof in relation to the Competition at any time before, during or after the Competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No entity other than FIFA may commercialise or exploit broadcast/recording/media rights without express FIFA authorisation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official FIFA TV and photo materials restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: FIFA has the sole and exclusive right to produce, record, exploit and further distribute film material for any commercial and non-commercial purposes, including documentaries related to the Competition and/or the participation of a Participating Club in the Competition, including all Team Delegation Members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless otherwise agreed in writing under a Participating Club Footage Licence Agreement, Participating Clubs shall not produce, record, exploit and/or distribute any audio-only, still or moving visual-only, audiovisual, data and/or textual material relating to FIFA, the Competition or ceremonies, for commercial or non-commercial purposes. Clubs must inform FIFA by the Team Workshop about planned content projects; FIFA will publish filming guidelines prior to the Competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive FIFA rights – Marketing
rubrics_metrics.description: FIFA has the sole and exclusive right to exploit all Marketing Rights in relation to the Competition. Neither the Member Associations nor the Participating Clubs, nor the Hosts, nor the Confederations, nor any third party may exploit any Marketing Rights or parts thereof in relation to the Competition at any time before, during or after the Competition Period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marketing initiatives referencing the Competition require FIFA approval or separate agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensing and merchandising subject to FIFA approval
rubrics_metrics.description: The Participating Clubs and FIFA may discuss and agree merchandising and licensing opportunities in respect of the Competition which shall, to the extent approved by FIFA, be subject to a separate agreement between FIFA and the relevant Participating Club.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any merchandising/licensing must be approved and is governed by separate contract terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment Regulations compliance and precedence
rubrics_metrics.description: During the Competition Period, each Participating Club must fully comply with the Equipment Regulations in their applicable form. In case of any inconsistency, these Media and Marketing Regulations shall take precedence over the terms of the Equipment Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clubs must follow Equipment Regulations but default to Media and Marketing Regulations where conflicts exist; 'clean site' principles apply in Controlled Areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor advertising on shirts – permitted conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition of sponsor advertising of a single Club Affiliate on Playing Equipment is permitted on the front of the Participating Club’s shirt, provided that: (a) the sponsor represents a single brand (no combination/composite branding); (b) the Club Affiliate is the club's main sponsor; (c) the sponsor advertising displayed corresponds to that displayed throughout the latest/current domestic season and/or the international club competition that qualified the club; (d) surface area does not exceed 200 cm² and is positioned on the front centre of the torso; (e) advertising of tobacco or strong alcoholic beverages and slogans of political, sexist, religious or racist nature or other offensive causes are strictly prohibited; (f) no Club Affiliate sponsor advertising is permitted on any other piece of Playing Equipment (except manufacturer in accordance with Equipment Regulations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict one-brand, area, position and content rules apply; matches domestic/international season appearance; prohibited categories enumerated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment and apparel coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: The Participating Club’s sports equipment must otherwise comply with the Equipment Regulations and all applicable laws of each Competition Territory. All restrictions on Playing Equipment set out in the Equipment Regulations shall also be deemed to apply to all apparel, Special Equipment items (items worn underneath Playing Equipment), and all items and apparel worn in replacement of Playing Equipment, including T-shirts and any 'celebratory' apparel worn/displayed by any Team Delegation Members during or following any Competition Match.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restrictions extend beyond primary playing kit to undergarments, replacement apparel and celebratory items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bags and further items branding restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: All bags and/or further items used by, or belonging to, Team Delegation Members brought into any Competition Stadium or media areas must be free of all branding other than (i) the official emblem of the Participating Club and (ii) the logo of the manufacturer. The maximum size of the manufacturer’s logo shall be 25 cm². No more than one manufacturer’s logo may appear on any such bag or further items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict limitation to club emblem and single small manufacturer logo for any bags/items in Controlled Areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal attire branding prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: All formal attire (such as ties, suits, dress shirts, accessory items, etc.) worn by the Team Delegation Members within the Controlled Areas must be completely free of third-party (neither commercial nor manufacturer) branding, other than the emblem of their Participating Club. The same restriction applies to both formal attire and Special Equipment items if formal attire is worn together with Special Equipment items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No third-party or manufacturer branding allowed on formal attire in Controlled Areas, except club emblem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of Equipment samples to FIFA
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to the Equipment Regulations, each Participating Club shall submit to FIFA, for FIFA’s approval, one sample of all Equipment items to be worn by its Team Delegation Members within the Controlled Areas during the Competition Period, namely all Playing Equipment, Special Equipment and further apparel worn in replacement of Playing Equipment (including any 'celebratory' apparel) and all formal attire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clubs must submit sample items by FIFA deadline for approval; FIFA will notify deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wearable technology testing, certification and data use limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Special items worn by players for performance-related purposes (e.g., electronic performance and tracking system devices) must be tested and certified by, or under the auspices of, FIFA subject to Law 4 of the Laws of the Game before they are allowed to be used during any Competition Match. Participating Clubs must inform FIFA and ensure devices are on FIFA's list of approved devices or in the testing/certification process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data collected may only be used by the respective club and/or the individual player for performance-monitoring purposes; any other use (especially commercial or disclosure to third parties/public) is strictly prohibited. Use inside the technical area is prohibited. Special items shall not display branding of manufacturer/third party except one tonal identification not visible while used. FIFA may impose further restrictions on collection/use/interpretation of such data.

rubrics_metrics.name: No advertising on Equipment and personal items in Controlled Areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise expressly permitted, all Team Delegation Members are prohibited from displaying any (i) commercial, political, religious or personal messages or slogans in any language, (ii) commercial branding, and/or (iii) manufacturer marks or name of any kind on their Playing Equipment, Special Equipment, formal attire, further apparel worn in replacement of Playing Equipment or other items used (including bags, ball bags, goalkeeping gloves, beverage containers and medical bags), or on their person for the duration of their stay in a Controlled Area on Matchdays and non-Matchdays. This includes personal items (hats, sunglasses, bags, luggage, headphones, fashion accessories).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comprehensive prohibition covering any visible messaging/branding on equipment and personal items while in Controlled Areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment branding exception for ball boys/girls and escorts
rubrics_metrics.description: Equipment items worn by ball boys and girls, player escorts and flagbearers during Competition Matches may display the branding of Commercial Partners as approved by FIFA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited exception to equipment branding rules for specific matchday roles, subject to FIFA approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: FIFA-provided technical equipment and controlled use
rubrics_metrics.description: FIFA will provide, upon arrival in a Competition Territory, specified technical items (two first-aid cases, plastic bottle carriers, one cooler, 50 plastic drinking bottles, 3 x 2 captain’s armbands, three ball bags, official Competition match balls). FIFA will also provide player warm-up/training bibs (bearing FIFA/FIFA.com/Competition branding) which must be used exclusively and returned after each Match or official training session.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except for training sessions at Official Training Sites (where non-Commercial Partner equipment may be permitted), Team Delegation Members are not permitted to use other items of the same or similar type in Controlled Areas. During training sessions at Official Training Site and Competition Stadium official training sessions, only the official match ball provided by a Commercial Partner may be used. Warm-up bibs provided by FIFA cannot be re-branded and must be returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beverage supply and competing brand prohibition in Controlled Areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Participating Clubs will be provided with products from The Coca-Cola Company, including water and sports drinks, for use in the Controlled Areas. If clubs wish to use beverage products manufactured by any other entity, they must be stored or contained in the plastic drinking bottles provided by FIFA prior to arrival. Participating Clubs are expressly prohibited from bringing beverage products of competitors of The Coca-Cola Company into the Controlled Areas unless such products are contained within the containers provided by FIFA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FIFA supplies beverages; competing beverage brands are disallowed in Controlled Areas absent FIFA container rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official Training Sites advertising restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise specifically confirmed in writing by FIFA, the only advertising permitted at the Official Training Sites is that of the Commercial Partners, to be erected by FIFA at its sole discretion. Participating Clubs must not display, arrange for the display of, or authorise the distribution of any advertising or other promotional materials at the Official Training Sites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clubs cannot place ads/promotional materials at Official Training Sites; FIFA manages permissible advertising.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attendance, ticketing and promotions at Official Training Sites
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise confirmed in writing by FIFA, all training sessions at Official Training Sites are controlled by FIFA and the LOC. No Participating Club, Club Affiliate or any third party contracted to a Participating Club may run any kind of promotion associated with attendance at a training session at an Official Training Site, nor sell or distribute tickets for attendance, in any commercial or non-commercial form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clubs must not monetise or promote attendance at Official Training Site training sessions; FIFA/LOC control access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor recognition on training shirts and warm-up bibs at Official Training Sites
rubrics_metrics.description: Training shirts, supplementary Equipment items and warm-up/training bibs worn by Team Delegation Members at Official Training Sites may display the branding of Club Affiliates or any third party contracted to the Participating Clubs (excluding official training sessions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited allowance for club-affiliate branding on training items at Official Training Sites except for official training sessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sales of food, beverages and merchandise at Official Training Sites
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise confirmed in writing by FIFA, with the exception of any arrangements made by FIFA with Commercial Partners, no third-party arrangements made by the Participating Clubs for food and beverages at the Official Training Sites are permitted. With the exception of arrangements made by FIFA or by third parties appointed by FIFA with official licensees, no third-party merchandise or licensing products shall be offered for sale or distributed at the Official Training Sites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commercial sales by clubs/third parties at Official Training Sites are prohibited unless expressly arranged by FIFA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media cooperation obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Participating Club must assist, and must ensure that each Team Delegation Member assists, to the best possible extent, FIFA, FIFA Content Production Crews, representatives of the Media Partners and accredited media representatives in their media activities during the Competition Period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clubs and delegation members must cooperate proactively with FIFA/media requests to support documentation, editorial coverage and promotion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to Participating Clubs and media liaison
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Participating Club shall appoint one Team Delegation Member as a liaison between the Participating Club and FIFA to act as team media officer. Each Participating Club grants FIFA and nominees the non-exclusive right to gain preferred access, for interview purposes, to all Team Delegation Members as reasonably requested. Clubs shall grant FIFA free access (subject to reasonable limits for privacy and sporting concerns) to areas where a club is training and/or staying from five days prior to the first Competition Match until 12 hours after the last Competition Match.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clubs must provide liaison, reasonable interview access, and allow FIFA access to training facilities, team hotels and media areas, balancing privacy/sporting concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability in pre-mixed zone and dressing room access rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Team Delegation Members must be available in the 'pre-mixed zone area' and designated Official Training Site areas for post-match and post-training interviews upon reasonable request. Notwithstanding general access, in respect only of the final Competition Match the winning Participating Club shall grant FIFA Content Production Crew access to its dressing room for filming/photography immediately following return to the dressing room after the match for approx. ten minutes for non-live filming/still photography. Permission to film dressing room celebrations for other matches is at the discretion of the Participating Clubs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clubs should make players available in designated mixed/pre-mixed zones. Dressing-room filming allowances are specified for final match winners and discretionary otherwise; privacy must be respected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Club Media Day and pre-Competition media activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Participating Clubs are requested to organise a 'Club Media Day' preferably 3-4 weeks before their first Competition Match or immediately after qualification if later. FIFA Content Production Crews, Media Partners and other FIFA representatives must be permitted access. Pre-Competition media activities are discretionary and subject to agreement with FIFA; these may include sit-down interviews (~20 minutes) with up to four players, short-form social content (~10 minutes), a coach interview (~20 minutes), a photography session (~10 minutes), and produced content may be used by FIFA and Media Partners to promote the Competition and for in-tournament delivery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clubs are asked to host Club Media Day and cooperate on pre-Competition media requests; all produced content may be used by FIFA/media for promotion and tournament delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrival-in-territory media obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: On the day of arrival in a Competition Territory (or on/before the day of arrival of the opposition), each Participating Club is obliged to hold Official FIFA/LOC Media Activities ensuring presence of its head coach and at least one player likely to be in starting XI. FIFA/host broadcaster may film arrivals; clubs shall provide opportunity. FIFA may request a video and photography session (not including interviews) lasting up to two hours with full squad in playing kit to be used for promotion and in-tournament delivery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clubs must facilitate arrival media activities, provide personnel and enable filming sessions as requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training session media access encouragement
rubrics_metrics.description: Before or after all training sessions (whether or not at a Competition Stadium), the Participating Club is encouraged to make its head coach and at least one player available to media representatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clubs should facilitate media access around training sessions to support media coverage, except where restricted by prior agreement or sporting/privacy concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official FIFA/LOC Media Activities at Competition Stadium – training access and press conference
rubrics_metrics.description: With the exception of one training session prior to each Competition Match, all training sessions shall be open to the media for at least 15 minutes following their commencement. Clubs shall inform FIFA in writing if they intend to exclude media after providing 15 minutes access. FIFA Officials/media will not be permitted onto the pitch. An official press conference and/or mixed zone will be organised by FIFA on the day preceding the Matchday following the official training session and must be attended by the club’s head coach and at least one player likely to be in starting XI. Attendance of a player at the press conference may be replaced by making at least three players available for interviews in a mixed-zone around the training pitch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clubs must provide 15 minutes' media access at training, attend pre-match press activities, and coordinate replacements if necessary; pitch entry by media is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matchday media activities and dressing-room filming for host broadcasters
rubrics_metrics.description: On Matchday, prior to arrival, the host broadcaster and an official photographer shall be granted access to the Participating Club’s dressing room for filming and photos (includes unilateral stand-up interviews by up to two Media Partners filmed by the host broadcaster). Upon arrival, the head coach or other Team Delegation members shall be available for 'upon arrival' interviews. After each Competition Match, interviews shall be given by the head coach and certain players as flash interviews on the pitch near the technical area and in the players’ tunnel or close to team dressing rooms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clubs must coordinate dressing-room filming/photo access pre-arrival, facilitate arrival interviews, and provide post-match flash interview availability at specified locations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-match obligations (press conference, Player of the Match and mixed zone)
rubrics_metrics.description: After each Competition Match: (a) the Participating Club’s head coach must attend the official post-match press conference, as must any player(s) receiving an individual award; (b) the player selected as 'Player of the Match' will be required to participate in related post-match activation including appearing for a photograph in front of the Presenting Partner’s backdrop and accepting the commercially branded trophy; (c) all players who took part must pass through the mixed zone after the final whistle to be available for interviews (mixed-zone activities should conclude no later than 60 minutes after the final whistle); (d) players selected for doping control must remain available for flash interviews immediately following the match, if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clubs must ensure coach and nominated players attend press activities and that players pass through the mixed zone within the specified time; award activations and doping-control availability have specific media requirements.
